To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the finite-element scheme and the finite-volume scheme converge to a weak solution of the coupled system.
the finite element and the finite volume methods are well-suited to the discretization of nonlinear coupled elliptic systems.

the discretization of coupled heat diffusion and electrical diffusion problems using finite-element and finite volume methods yields approximate solutions which converge to a solution of a coupled system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discretization of a system of nonlinear elliptic partial differential equations.

the following topics: 1) the existence, uniqueness, regularity and approximation of solutions of the coupled heat and electrical problems; 2) a priori error estimates for the finite-element and finite volume methods; 3) the numerical solution of coupled heat and diffusion problems.

the following topics: - The mathematical analysis of coupled heat and electric diffusion models; - The development of numerical algorithms for the discretization in space of these models; - The convergence analysis of these algorithms; - The development and the use of numerical methods for the solution of the resulting systems of algebraic equations; - The numerical analysis of these methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the finite-volume method is the method of choice for the solution of the coupled problem.
the finite-element and finite- volume schemes are convergent for the solution of the coupled system, provided that the solution is sufficiently smooth.
the finite-volume scheme is more robust than the finite-element one in the case of the coupled heat and electrical problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the coupled problem has a solution and that the approximate solution of the discretized problem converges to a solution of that problem.

, in the context of coupled heat and electricity diffusion, the finite-volume and finite-element schemes are equivalent in the sense that the convergence properties of the approximate solutions are the same for both schemes.
the finite-element method is more accurate than the finite-volume method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even in the case of a strongly coupled nonlinear system of elliptics, a finite-element scheme and finite-volume scheme can be used for discretization.
the convergence of the approximate solution is obtained by a compactness argument, without any a priori assumption on the regularity of the solution.
the finite-element scheme is more accurate than the finite-volume scheme, but both are convergent.
